hypothesis: The selected evidence-routed portfolio can unify four-asset HYPE-breakout observation into the account-owning backend and TUI without widening its two executable mappings, adding per-provider venue candle requests, or allowing observe-only conflicts to alter executable routing.
decision: Retain v10 as the preferred inactive next-flat candidate. Source tracing and focused integration tests now establish that unauthorized provider-symbol intents are removed before same-symbol conflict ranking and portfolio-capacity accounting. A deliberately higher-priority observe-only HYPE/BTC short neither suppressed an executable Hulk/BTC long nor closed an existing executable long. The current live runtime remains unchanged while HYPE is open.
falsifier: A changed candidate or runner source identity, any executable mapping beyond Hulk/BTC and HYPE-breakout/HYPE, any observe-only intent changing an executable action, position capacity, or close decision, added per-provider venue fetching, missing four-asset collector coverage, or a failed next-flat transition invalidates selection or routing isolation.
limitations: V10 has not run as the authenticated account-owning backend.
The routing tests use deterministic protocol fakes rather than venue orders.
Four-asset observation does not establish transferable strategy edge or profitability.
Historical unchanged transfers remain negative for ETH and SOL and contradictory for BTC.
The current open HYPE lifecycle remains governed by its original profile and in-memory implementation.
The one-time legacy cutover retains a documented flat-to-STOP entry race because the current process lacks transition-drain support.
